title: Pointed etale spans descend with both target families fixed
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $B=\varprojlim_i S_i$ and projections $p_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Fix $b\in B$, put $s_i=p_i(b)$, and assume each induced map $\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(b)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-residue-field]. Fix $i_0\in I$ and affine schemes $P_0,Q_0$ of finite presentation over $S_{i_0}$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $j\geq i_0$ set $P_j=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_j$, $Q_j=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_j$, and put $P_B=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$, $Q_B=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $U$ is affine of finite presentation over $B$, $u\in U$ lies over $b$, and $a:U\to P_B$, $c:U\to Q_B$ are etale $B$-morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] inducing isomorphisms $\kappa(a(u))\to\kappa(u)$ and $\kappa(c(u))\to\kappa(u)$. Then there exist $j\geq i_0$, an affine scheme $U_j$ of finite presentation over $S_j$, etale $S_j$-morphisms $a_j:U_j\to P_j$, $c_j:U_j\to Q_j$, and a $B$-isomorphism $e:U_j\times_{S_j}B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ such that $a\circ e$ and $c\circ e$ are the actual base changes of $a_j$ and $c_j$. Let $u_j$ be the projection of $e^{-1}(u)$, and let $x_j,y_j$ be the images of $a(u),c(u)$ in the fixed models $P_j,Q_j$. Then $a_j(u_j)=x_j$, $c_j(u_j)=y_j$, and the canonical maps $\kappa(x_j)\to\kappa(a(u))$, $\kappa(y_j)\to\kappa(c(u))$, and $\kappa(u_j)\to\kappa(u)$ are isomorphisms. In particular both stage arrows are elementary at $u_j$, meaning their induced residue-field maps are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, affine case and clauses (1),(2); Tag 07RP, lemma-descend-etale; pointed refinement for the fixed-family descent in more-morphisms.tex, Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, third paragraph.

proof.text: Restrict the system to $I_{\ge i_0}$. It still has limit $B$: given a compatible cone on this tail, its component at an arbitrary $i$ is obtained by choosing $k\ge i,i_0$ and composing the component at $k$ with $S_k\to S_i$; a common upper bound proves independence of $k$ and compatibility, and also proves uniqueness. The same argument permits restriction to any later tail below. Every transition map is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since its source and target are affine. Each $S_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the limit $B$ is affine. These verify the inverse-system hypotheses for finite-presentation descent.

Apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $U\to B$ on this tail. Obtain $r\ge i_0$, a morphism $V_r\to S_r$ of finite presentation, and a $B$-isomorphism $e_r:V_r\times_{S_r}B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. Since $S_r$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $V_r\to S_r$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $V_r$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No target scheme has been descended or replaced.

The base change of $V_r\to S_r$ to $B$ is affine: through $e_r$ it is $U\to B$, a morphism between affine schemes, so use [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-affine] to $V_r\to S_r$; its three initial schemes $S_r,V_r,S_r$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by steps 1 and 2. At a later stage $r'$, $V_r\times_{S_r}S_{r'}\to S_{r'}$ is affine, so its source is affine by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. It is still of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Replace $r,V_r,e_r$ by this stage, source, and the induced isomorphism to $U$; the latter uses the canonical iterated-pullback isomorphism from the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product].

The specified schemes $P_r=P_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_r$ and $Q_r=Q_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_r$ are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and of finite presentation over $S_r$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out] (2), separately, to the two $B$-morphisms $a\circ e_r$ and $c\circ e_r$ from $(V_r)_B$ to $(P_r)_B=P_B$ and $(Q_r)_B=Q_B$. Choose a common upper bound $k$ of the two resulting stages and base change both arrows to it. Set $U_k=V_r\times_{S_r}S_k$. We obtain $S_k$-morphisms $a_k:U_k\to P_k$ and $c_k:U_k\to Q_k$ whose base changes are $a\circ e_k,c\circ e_k$, with $e_k:(U_k)_B\cong U$ induced by $e_r$. All identifications with the fixed $P_k,Q_k,P_B,Q_B$ are the unique iterated-pullback comparisons preserving projections [def-pc-fibre-product]; hence these equations concern the actual pullback arrows. The source $U_k$ is affine and finitely presented over $S_k$ by the same two cited permanence statements.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (2); More on Morphisms Tag 0GDX, finite-stage span paragraph

proof.text:
Check the local finite presentation needed for etaleness descent, without assuming it descends automatically for an arbitrary arrow. Write $R=\Gamma(S_k,\mathcal O)$, $C=\Gamma(U_k,\mathcal O)$, and $D=\Gamma(P_k,\mathcal O)$ (and then repeat with $Q_k$). Since both structure maps to $S_k$ are locally of finite presentation, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives presentations $C=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ and $D=R[t_1,\ldots,t_v]/(h_1,\ldots,h_w)$. Choose polynomials $F_i(x)$ representing the images of $t_i$ under $D\to C$. Then
$$C\cong D[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m,t_1-F_1(x),\ldots,t_v-F_v(x)).$$
Indeed substitution $t_i=F_i(x)$ and the map sending $x_l$ to its class give inverse maps: each $h_l(F(x))$ already lies in $(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ because $D\to C$ is a ring map. This is a finite presentation over $D$. The full affine source and target are the neighbourhoods in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so both $a_k$ and $c_k$ are locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, and 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence (1), affine argument written out

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-etale] twice, to $a_k$ and $c_k$ over the tail starting at $k$. Its initial source, target and base are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; step 5 supplies local finite presentation and the limit arrows are the given etale arrows. Choose $j$ above the two resulting indices. Both arrows remain etale after this further base change by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Set $U_j=U_k\times_{S_k}S_j$ and let $a_j,c_j$ be these pullbacks, retaining the fixed $P_j,Q_j$. The source is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and of finite presentation over $S_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Let $e:(U_j)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ be $e_k$ composed with the iterated-pullback comparison [def-pc-fibre-product]. The two equations from step 4 continue to hold, since the composites with each pullback projection agree and the universal property determines the induced maps uniquely.

proof.text: Put $z=e^{-1}(u)$ and let $u_j$ be its image in $U_j$. The point $z$ lies over $b$, since $e$ is over $B$. Evaluate the two pullback equations at $z$: the first gives $a_j(u_j)=x_j$ and the second $c_j(u_j)=y_j$, with $x_j,y_j$ exactly the projections specified in the statement. All three stage points lie over $s_j$, by the commutative squares defining the pullbacks [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, point u_i and its images

proof.text: Compare the fibres over $b$ and $s_j$ for each of the three cartesian pairs $(U_j,(U_j)_B)$, $(P_j,P_B)$ and $(Q_j,Q_B)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] the map between the fibres is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s_j)$. This is an isomorphism by hypothesis; its inverse induces the inverse between the two fibre products by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The fibre projections induce isomorphisms on point residue fields by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-residue-field-iso]: all the schemes here are affine, and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies a fibre with the spectrum of its coordinate ring tensored with the base residue field. Consequently the canonical residue-field map from a stage point to its given limit point is an isomorphism: write $\alpha_s:\kappa(v_j)\to\kappa(v_{s_j})$ and $\alpha_b:\kappa(v_B)\to\kappa(v_b)$ for the two fibre-projection residue maps, and $h^\kappa:\kappa(v_{s_j})\to\kappa(v_b)$ for the fibre-isomorphism residue map. If $\gamma:\kappa(v_j)\to\kappa(v_B)$ is the canonical map, commutativity gives $\alpha_b\circ\gamma=h^\kappa\circ\alpha_s$, hence $\gamma=\alpha_b^{-1}\circ h^\kappa\circ\alpha_s$. Applied to $u_j,x_j,y_j$, and identifying $\kappa(z)$ with $\kappa(u)$ through $e$, this gives all three asserted canonical isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 02V3, proof fibre-base-change display; Algebra Tag 0H9M, remark-local-ring-fibre; pointed field comparison in More on Morphisms Tag 0GDX

proof.text: Functoriality of the induced residue maps [def-weil-residue-field] gives the commutative square with top arrow $\kappa(x_j)\to\kappa(u_j)$, bottom arrow $\kappa(a(u))\to\kappa(u)$, and vertical arrows the canonical isomorphisms of step 8. The bottom arrow is an isomorphism by hypothesis. Thus the top arrow equals the bottom arrow conjugated by the two vertical isomorphisms and is an isomorphism. The identical square with $y_j,c(u)$ proves that $c_j$ also induces an isomorphism at $u_j$. Together with step 6, these are the two required elementary etale arrows, and all the asserted data and identities have been constructed.
